clue.text: South American girl worth a close look

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A Latin American woman is admired as being worth inspecting closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination of something.

clue.text: In a word, look before you leap

definitions.text: In a word, look before you leap

parts.words: In a word, look before you leap
parts.note: the famous piece of advice is summed up in one word naming what kind of saying it is, with a hint at being pro (for) the word

explanation.surface: Summing up a familiar piece of advice about caution in one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Look before you leap is a well-known saying, an example of traditional wisdom in a short phrase.

clue.text: Lots of pies made from puree

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the word puree, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of pies are being cooked using puree.
explanation.walkthrough: The pie was a small Indian coin, a fraction of the currency unit, so 'lots of pies' adds up to the answer; the surface wants pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: The pie was a small coin of British India, many of which made up one Indian currency unit.

clue.text: Undisciplined pets made herd scatter wildly

indicators.note: undisciplined letters are unruly and out of order, so the words pets made are rearranged

explanation.surface: Badly trained animals cause a herd to bolt in panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of a herd of animals.

clue.text: Too thin to stand up?

parts.note: someone very skinny, and also a way of standing that is not fully upright but propped against something

explanation.surface: Someone so skinny they can barely stay on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both thin and slim, and to rest at an angle against a support rather than stand straight.

clue.text: Canine compilers

definitions.meaning: dogs, specifically gundogs of a breed such as the Irish red

explanation.definitionFit: Setters are a breed of gundog, and crossword compilers are also called setters.

clue.text: Tied up and after a time, wrapped, say?

indicators.note: the word for tied up is placed after the word for a time

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: Someone tied up and, after a while, wrapped in a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: 'wrapped' sounds like rapt, which means enthralled; the 'say?' flags the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enthralled or entranced, as if under a magic charm, is a state of rapt attention.

clue.text: Girl playing Hamlet

indicators.note: playing with the letters of Hamlet means rearranging them

explanation.surface: An actress is taking the role of the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Poor Noel gets stage fright — pulls out

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Poor Noel gets stage fright — pulls out', gives anagram fodder NOELGETS, one A short of the answer; no word supplies the A.
annotationWithheld.clue: Poor Noel gets stage fright — pulls out

clue.text: Profligate poet?

definitions.meaning: Stephen ... was an English poet of the 1930s generation

explanation.definitionFit: A wasteful person who spends freely, and the surname of the poet Stephen Spender.

clue.text: Hang a rope from this building

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of hang a rope, rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to suspend a rope from some building.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a home for children without parents.

clue.text: Run off, in East European retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters for East European are read in reverse

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Fleeing to a hideaway somewhere in Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns EPOLE round to give the answer; it looks like a noun for a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: Release banker and politician given time

parts.note: a banker is crossword code for a river (it has banks); the Exe is a river in Devon, England
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A financier and an MP are let off after serving their sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier but a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation or duty.

clue.text: Birds are, when fruit gets past its best

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
aged means old, past its prime

explanation.surface: A remark on what happens when fruit goes past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are covered in feathers, so they could be described as feathered.

clue.text: Simply got a change, not being single-minded

indicators.note: the letters of simply got a get a change, that is, are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone simply changed their mind and lost their single focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single-minded' is a pun: the answer is someone with a mind to more than one spouse, not unfocused.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with more than one spouse at a time is not content with one partner.

clue.text: Most unlikely to be a stone!

definitions.text: Most unlikely to be a stone!

parts.words: Most unlikely to be a stone!
parts.note: plays on the saying that you cannot get blood out of a stone, so a stone is the last thing to give some

explanation.surface: Something that seems least likely to be a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives blood is the opposite of a stone, from which proverbially none can be drawn.

clue.text: Load never shifted — too heavily weighed down

indicators.note: the letters of load never are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A load that has never been moved is weighing too heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means carrying too heavy a burden.

clue.text: Whisk in jug

definitions.meaning: to whisk is to mix by beating

explanation.definitionFit: To beat or mix a liquid, and a slang term for prison, as is jug.

clue.text: To catch a salmon, takes ten, reeling

indicators.note: reeling means spinning or staggering, so the letters of takes ten are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Landing a salmon takes ten turns of the reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeling' looks like the angler at work but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake-net is a fishing net fixed on stakes, used especially for salmon.

clue.text: Knock back these dregs of liquor and at one time you'd get blind

indicators.note: knocking back means turning round, so the old word for blind is read backwards

parts.note: to seel is an old falconry verb, used at one time, meaning to blind a hawk by stitching its eyelids

explanation.surface: Downing the last of the drink, which in the old days might leave you blind drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at one time' signals that SEEL is an archaic word; reversed it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment left at the bottom of a wine bottle or cask.

clue.text: Generous yet derogatory about an artist

indicators.note: the word for a derogatory statement goes about, that is around, the artist

parts.note: a libel is a derogatory published statement
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Someone is kind, though they make disparaging remarks about a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means giving freely, open-handed.

clue.text: Sent off, with a wave of the hand?

definitions.text: Sent off, with a wave of the hand?

parts.words: Sent off, with a wave of the hand?
parts.note: sent off reads as dismissed with a wave, but means sent off to sleep by the passes of a mesmerist's hand

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed with a casual wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesmerist puts a subject into a trance, traditionally with hand movements.

clue.text: Make you bulge? The gun concealed inside did!

indicators.note: the gun is hidden within the word did, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A hidden gun made a pocket bulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell out or cause to bulge.

clue.text: Poor little creature

parts.note: the saying as poor as a ... names a small animal living in a place of worship

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a pitiable small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom poor as a church mouse describes extreme poverty, using a tiny rodent in a chapel.

clue.text: At sea bed a hulk's piece of partitioning

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of bed a hulk are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Part of an old ship's hull lying on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulkhead is a dividing wall within a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Politician, runners held, is cutting corners

indicators.note: the politician is held inside the word for runners

parts.note: skis are runners for travelling over snow
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP who keeps athletes on is economising.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise by doing less than is needed.

clue.text: See 21
Smell, it's said, this river!

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word for smell is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: an odour is a smell

explanation.surface: Complaining about the stench of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river of central Europe forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: A help in locating girl in a car?

indicators.note: the girl is placed in the car

parts.note: RR, for Rolls-Royce, stands for a car
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl sitting in a car might help find the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a system for detecting the position of objects using radio waves.

clue.text: False teeth put in before contract

indicators.note: the word in is put before the word for false teeth

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: Getting false teeth fitted before signing an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal legal agreement, especially binding an apprentice.

clue.text: Summarily, hang space visitor on hillside terrace

parts.note: to lynch is to execute summarily, without trial
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A mob strings up an alien on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynchet is a bank or ridge of earth formed on a slope by ancient ploughing.

clue.text: English trader turned out film much the same as the one before

definitions.text: film much the same as the one before

indicators.note: turned out means reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British merchant produced a movie that repeated its predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a derivative remake, repeating an earlier work.
